tokyo_marugoto_vegan_dining_as.price_note: ⚠ NO DISHES OR PRICES — the menu is published as hashed PNG images with no alt text, so not one item name is readable. That is genuinely frustrating here, because THIS IS THE MOST IMPORTANT RESTAURANT IN THE TOKYO SET FOR BOTH DIETS AT ONCE and the shop documents its own policy in more detail than any other record in this dataset. What follows is that policy, quoted, and it is worth more than a dish list. Tabelog not consulted: it has served Cf-Mitigated: challenge (HTTP 403) to this egress since 2026-09-02. ⚠ THE CLAIM: the shop states 「店内提供料理及び、店内販売商品は全てグルテンを使用していない食品です」 — every dish served in the restaurant and every product sold in it is made without gluten — and the site header carries 全料理メニューグルテンフリー(小麦不使用). It is simultaneously an all-plant kitchen: 「全てのお料理に、アルコール及び豚肉の使用はございません」, and 五葷 (garlic, spring onion, onion, nira, rakkyo) are excluded from EVERY dine-in dish, which is the Buddhist 精進 standard and goes further than veganism does. A restaurant that is vegan, wheat-free and allium-free by policy is close to unique. ⚠ AND THE SHOP ITSELF REFUSES THE STRONGER CLAIM, WHICH IS WHY THIS RECORD IS "high" AND NOT "dedicated": 「完全にグルテンフリー対応のレストランとして運営しているわけではないため」 — we are NOT operated as a fully gluten-free restaurant. The specific gap they name is the honest one: 「製造時に工場でのコンタミネーションの有無については、確認していません」 — for bought-in seasonings and sauces they have NOT verified whether cross-contamination occurred at the factory. So the recipes contain no wheat; the supply chain is unaudited. That is exactly the distinction between an ingredient statement and a safety guarantee that RAKERU’s allergen page also drew, and this shop draws it voluntarily and in the customer’s favour. ⚠ TWO CARVE-OUTS THAT MATTER AND ARE EASY TO MISS. First: BEER. The menu page states 「ビール・ノンアルコールビールは小麦の使用あり」 — the beer AND the non-alcoholic beer contain WHEAT. In a restaurant where a coeliac can safely order literally everything on the food menu, the drinks list is where the wheat is, which is the reverse of every other record here. Second: the FROZEN RETAIL products sold in-store and online are NOT held to the dine-in 五葷 rule and may contain garlic — so the packet you buy on the way out is not governed by the policy that governs the plate you just ate. ⚠ ON HALAL: no pork and no alcohol in any dish, but alcohol IS used to sanitise equipment and tableware, and the seasonings are not halal-certified; the shop asks customers to judge for themselves rather than claiming certification. ⚠ RECORD-LEVEL NOTE FOR THE HUMAN GATE: on this evidence the tier fields for this shop are probably understated, but an upgrade of gf_confidence or vegan_status is a human decision under the asymmetry rule and is not made here. The published menu sections are Morning, Lunch, Dinner and Kids; re-check if the shop ever publishes the menu as text.

tokyo_igaya.price_note: 伊賀屋 (千代田区三崎町2-12-8, Suidōbashi) publishes its whole à la carte, sake and shochu shelves and its lunch on its own Gnavi shop site. The house sells live fish: the 極上！！刺身盛合わせ at ¥1,100 for seven pieces per person is listed with the day's provenance spelled out — 本鮪, 平目（青森）, 〆鯖（長崎）, カンパチ（五島列島）, カンヌキ（竹岡）, 活アオリイカ（山口）, 甘エビ（北海道）, 活鯵（勝山）, 金目鯛（勝浦）, カワハギ肝合え（大分）— and the shop says the fish were alive that day. ⚠ COURSES ARE UNPRICED SAMPLES, not fixed menus: the shop labels its ten-plate banquet listings 「季節や仕入れの状況により内容が変わります。下記はある日の一例です」— one particular day's line-up. The two figures it does publish for courses are a ¥7,350 course reduced to ¥6,600 with a coupon, a ぶりしゃぶ/金目鯛しゃぶ course from ¥5,500 by advance reservation, and a ¥2,000 all-you-can-drink add-on running from bottled beer through sake. Banquets take 4 people minimum. ⚠ GLUTEN: sashimi with soy, カレーうどん twice on the menu (wheat noodle plus wheat-thickened roux), 海鮮チヂミ (wheat batter), 海老フライ and ロースカツ (panko), 天ぷら, and the 伊賀ドレ house dressing on the green salad is undeclared. The one plate that stands out as worth asking about is グリーンアスパラ塩茹で at ¥330 — salt-boiled asparagus, nothing else named.
